problem: Prior visual navigation methods memorize raw perceptual features as episodic memory and treat memory and reasoning (long-term experience priors) as separate modules. Their very different representations make integrating the two for decision-making hard.
motivation: Embodied agents in large workspaces need both episodic spatio-temporal memory and proactive probabilistic reasoning over task distributions from long-term experience. A unified representation of the two could improve decision-making in image-goal navigation.
key_idea: Represent both memory (observed object sequences) and reasoning (a semantic object-relation graph) at the semantic level in one Semantic-based Multi-modal Cognitive Graph (SMCG), and decode both with a hierarchical cognition extraction pipeline.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The claimed reason it works is that moving memory and reasoning into a shared semantic (object-level) space lets heterogeneous cognitive cues be used together, and the gains are attributed to inducing and applying both modalities.
method: SMCG memory: stores sequences of observed objects instead of perceptual features, forming semantic-level episodic memory
Semantic relation graph: encodes correlations among objects, providing long-term-experience-based probabilistic reasoning
Unified semantic representation: memory and reasoning share the same semantic level, so they can be combined
Hierarchical cognition extraction (HCE): a pipeline that decodes cognitive cues from SMCG and from situation-aware subgraphs to drive navigation behavior
